compute.disks.create: To create the disks that exocompute uses to restore or archive protected data.
compute.disks.createSnapshot: To create a snapshot of a disk, so its data can be protected.
compute.disks.delete: To delete a disk exocompute created, once it is no longer needed.
compute.disks.get: To get a disk, so an unused name can be chosen for a new disk.
compute.disks.list: To list the disks in the project, so the disks of an instance can be found.
compute.disks.setLabels: To set labels on a disk, so Rubrik can identify it.
compute.disks.use: To use a disk, so it can be attached to an instance.
compute.globalOperations.get: To get the status of global operations, such as creating a network.
compute.instances.detachDisk: To detach a disk from an instance during a restore.
compute.instances.get: To get an instance, so the disks attached to it can be found before they are detached.
compute.networks.list: To list the VPC networks that exocompute can be set up on.
compute.projects.get: To get the project, so the host project of a shared VPC can be found.
compute.regionOperations.get: To get the status of regional operations, such as creating a subnet.
compute.snapshots.create: To create a snapshot of a disk.
compute.snapshots.delete: To delete a snapshot once it is no longer needed.
compute.snapshots.get: To get the status and details of a snapshot.
compute.snapshots.setLabels: To set labels on a snapshot, so Rubrik can identify it.
compute.snapshots.useReadOnly: To use a snapshot as the read-only source of a disk.
compute.zoneOperations.get: To get the status of zonal operations, such as creating a disk.
container.clusterRoleBindings.create: To create the cluster role bindings that give exocompute components cluster-wide access.
container.clusterRoleBindings.delete: To delete a cluster role binding that exocompute created.
container.clusterRoleBindings.get: To get a cluster role binding, so it can be reused or checked.
container.clusterRoleBindings.update: To update a cluster role binding that exocompute created.
container.clusterRoles.bind: To bind a cluster role that grants more access than Rubrik holds itself.
container.clusterRoles.create: To create the cluster roles that exocompute components use.
container.clusterRoles.delete: To delete a cluster role that exocompute created.
container.clusterRoles.escalate: To create cluster roles whose rules exceed the access Rubrik holds itself.
container.clusterRoles.get: To get a cluster role, so it can be reused or checked.
container.clusterRoles.update: To update a cluster role that exocompute created.
container.clusters.create: To create the GKE cluster that runs exocompute.
container.configMaps.create: To create the config maps that exocompute components read their settings from.
container.configMaps.get: To get a config map, so it can be reused or checked.
container.configMaps.list: To list the config maps in a namespace.
container.configMaps.update: To update a config map that exocompute created.
container.daemonSets.create: To create the daemon sets that run exocompute agents on every node.
container.daemonSets.delete: To delete a daemon set that exocompute created.
container.daemonSets.get: To get a daemon set, so it can be reused or checked.
container.daemonSets.getStatus: To get the rollout status of a daemon set.
container.daemonSets.update: To update a daemon set that exocompute created.
container.deployments.create: To create the deployments that run exocompute components.
container.deployments.delete: To delete a deployment that exocompute created.
container.deployments.get: To get a deployment, so it can be reused or checked.
container.deployments.getStatus: To get the rollout status of a deployment.
container.deployments.rollback: To restore a previous revision of a deployment.
container.events.get: To get a Kubernetes event, so a failure can be explained.
container.events.list: To list the Kubernetes events of pods, nodes and namespaces, so failures can be explained.
container.namespaces.create: To create the namespaces that hold exocompute workloads.
container.namespaces.get: To get a namespace, so it can be reused or checked.
container.namespaces.getStatus: To get the status of a namespace.
container.namespaces.list: To list the namespaces in the cluster.
container.namespaces.update: To update a namespace that exocompute created.
container.namespaces.updateStatus: To update the status of a namespace.
container.nodes.create: To create node objects in the cluster.
container.nodes.delete: To delete a node object from the cluster.
container.nodes.get: To get a node, so its state can be checked.
container.nodes.getStatus: To get the status of a node.
container.nodes.list: To list the nodes in the cluster, so their state can be checked.
container.operations.get: To get the status of GKE operations, such as creating or deleting a cluster.
container.persistentVolumeClaims.create: To create the volume claims that give workloads their storage.
container.persistentVolumeClaims.delete: To delete a volume claim once its workload finishes.
container.persistentVolumeClaims.get: To get a volume claim, so its state can be checked.
container.persistentVolumeClaims.update: To update a volume claim that exocompute created.
container.persistentVolumes.create: To create the persistent volumes that back workload storage with disks.
container.persistentVolumes.delete: To delete a persistent volume once its workload finishes.
container.persistentVolumes.get: To get a persistent volume, so its state can be checked.

container.pods.create: To create the pods that run exocompute workloads.
container.pods.delete: To delete a pod once its workload finishes.
container.pods.evict: To remove a pod from a node by evicting it.
container.pods.exec: To access a running pod, so commands can be run in it.

container.pods.getStatus: To get the status of a pod.

container.pods.list: To list the pods in a namespace, so their state can be checked.
container.pods.portForward: To use port forwarding to reach a pod.
container.pods.proxy: To access a pod through the Kubernetes API proxy.
container.pods.update: To update a pod that exocompute created.
container.pods.updateStatus: To update the status of a pod.

container.replicaSets.get: To get a replica set, so its state can be checked.

container.replicaSets.getStatus: To get the status of a replica set.
container.replicaSets.list: To list the replica sets in a namespace.
container.replicaSets.update: To update a replica set that exocompute created.
container.roleBindings.create: To create the role bindings that give exocompute components access in a namespace.
container.roleBindings.delete: To delete a role binding that exocompute created.
container.roleBindings.get: To get a role binding, so it can be reused or checked.
container.roleBindings.list: To list the role bindings in a namespace.
container.roleBindings.update: To update a role binding that exocompute created.
container.roles.bind: To bind a role that grants more access than Rubrik holds itself.
container.roles.create: To create the roles that exocompute components use in a namespace.
container.roles.delete: To delete a role that exocompute created.
container.roles.escalate: To create roles whose rules exceed the access Rubrik holds itself.
container.roles.get: To get a role, so it can be reused or checked.

container.roles.update: To update a role that exocompute created.
container.secrets.create: To create the secrets that exocompute components use, such as credentials.
container.secrets.get: To get a secret, so it can be reused or checked.

container.secrets.update: To update a secret that exocompute created.

container.serviceAccounts.get: To get a service account, so it can be reused or checked.

container.services.get: To get a service, so it can be reused or checked.

container.clusters.delete: To delete the exocompute GKE cluster when it is torn down or its setup fails.
container.clusters.get: To get the state and settings of the exocompute GKE cluster.
